data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The sum of all possible values of n is 16592.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A prime power p^20 exists below 12005 (not possible as 2^20 > 10^6).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A prime combination p^6 * q^2 exists where p >= 5 and m < 12005 (not possible as 5^6 = 15625).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The number of positive factors of an integer m = p1^a1 * p2^a2... is given by d(m) = (a1+1)(a2+1)... For d(m) = 21, the prime factorization of m = n + 2005 must be either m = p^20 or m = p^6 * q^2. Since 2^20 > 12005, only the form m = p^6 * q^2 is viable within the range 2006 <= m < 12005. Testing p=2 yields m = 64 * q^2; for 2006 <= 64*q^2 < 12005, q must be a prime in [6, 13], giving q = {7, 11, 13} and m = {3136, 7744, 10816}. Testing p=3 yields m = 729 * q^2; for 2006 <= 729*q^2 < 12005, q must be a prime in [2, 3], but q != p, so q = 2, giving m = 2916. For p >= 5, p^6 * q^2 exceeds 12005. The possible values for n = m - 2005 are {1131, 5739, 8811, 911}.
